targetAudience.primary: Engineers building agent runtimes, plugin hosts, tool workers and crash-recovery protocols
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands process isolation, retries, durable logs and external tool effects.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A restarted plugin cannot tell whether an operation never ran, ran without acknowledgement, or already settled unless authoritative recovery facts survive elsewhere.

whyNow: A primary process-isolation study reports recovery through selected process kills by combining an external append-only transcript, stable call identity and durable-before-visible settlement while retaining at-least-once delivery and external-effect limits.

externalHook.description: A disposable process is recoverable only when the facts that authorize replay survive outside its failure domain.

coreProposition: Process isolation becomes trustworthy recovery only when session truth, stable effect identity, durable-before-visible settlement, and ownership generations survive outside the failed worker; effects beyond that represented boundary still require independent provider-side evidence.

originalValue.description: Separates blast-radius containment from replay authority and identifies the durable truth and external-effect evidence each boundary requires.

readerTakeaway: Externalize session truth and stable effect identity, record represented settlement before downstream visibility, track ownership generations, and use provider receipts or idempotency evidence for effects outside the transcript boundary.

supported: The reported system stores session truth in an append-only transcript outside peer processes.
Its protocol uses stable call identities and durable-before-visible settlement under at-least-once control delivery.
The study reports successful recovery across selected process-kill trials without repeating represented settled effects.
unsupported: Exactly-once execution for arbitrary external actions
uncertain: How the transcript should survive machine loss and corruption
How provider commit receipts should close the external-effect crash window

firstPartyRole.rationale: The recovery boundary is general to plugin and worker architectures.

decisionReason: The architecture and bounded fault experiments support a concrete distinction between process isolation, durable replay authority and external-effect certainty.
